title: Aqarios Launches Constraint-Native Quantum Optimizer in the IBM Qiskit Functions Catalog - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Aqarios released its Constrained Quantum Optimizer (FlexQAOA/IWS-QAOA) in IBM's Qiskit Functions Catalog, enforcing one-hot and set-packing constraints natively in-circuit instead of via penalty terms. On IBM Heron hardware it hit 100% feasible optima on MIS and Max-4-Cut benchmarks and cut QPU time from 130-200 s to about 30 s by dropping variational training, though no classical baseline is given.

themes.theme: Aqarios lands on IBM Qiskit catalog

insights.claim: Munich-based LMU Munich spin-off Aqarios GmbH has released its Constrained Quantum Optimizer as a managed solver in the IBM Qiskit Functions Catalog, available to IBM Quantum Premium, Flex, and on-premises users for discrete combinatorial optimization.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IBM's Functions Catalog is becoming a distribution channel for third-party quantum software startups, deepening the IBM Quantum ecosystem moat for paying enterprise tiers.
insights.locator: Aqarios GmbH, a Munich-based quantum software spin-off

insights.claim: Aqarios' Constrained Quantum Optimizer accepts standard LP, MPS, or Luna Model files, letting users feed conventional optimization model formats directly to a quantum solver.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Compatibility with standard OR file formats lowers integration friction for enterprises already using classical solvers, a prerequisite for quantum optimization adoption.
insights.quote: ingests standard LP, MPS, or Luna Model files
insights.locator: Aqarios GmbH, a Munich-based quantum software spin-off

insights.claim: Aqarios' optimizer is built on its FlexQAOA engine, whose approach has been validated in a peer-reviewed New Journal of Physics study.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Peer-reviewed validation is a differentiator among quantum software startups whose claims are often marketing-only.
insights.locator: Aqarios GmbH, a Munich-based quantum software spin-off

insights.claim: Conventional quantum optimization converts constrained problems into unconstrained binary models via quadratic penalty weights, which expands the effective search space and requires manual tuning.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Penalty-based encodings are a key scaling bottleneck for near-term quantum optimization; approaches that avoid them address a real weakness.
insights.quote: adding penalty weights that expand the effective search space and require manual tuning
insights.locator: Conventional quantum optimization workflows translate constrained problems

insights.claim: Aqarios enforces hard one-hot and set-packing constraints natively at the circuit level using Iterative Warm-Start XY-Mixer QAOA (IWS-QAOA), which confines state evolution to the feasible Hamming-weight-1 subspace rather than relying solely on penalty terms.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Constraint-native circuit design is a technical path to higher feasibility rates on noisy hardware; watch whether other Qiskit Functions providers adopt similar mixers.
insights.quote: confine state evolution to the feasible Hamming-weight-1 subspace
insights.locator: Conventional quantum optimization workflows translate constrained problems

insights.claim: IWS-QAOA uses fixed linear-ramp schedules to eliminate variational parameter training loops on quantum hardware.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Removing variational training loops cuts QPU time, the main cost driver for cloud quantum users.
insights.quote: eliminate variational parameter training loops on quantum hardware
insights.locator: Conventional quantum optimization workflows translate constrained problems

insights.claim: Before circuit synthesis, Aqarios' automated preprocessor compresses qubit counts via graph clique merging and pendant-node variable fixing, converts remaining constraints with structure-derived penalty weights, and repairs noise-induced constraint violations with greedy steepest-descent post-processing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Much of the practical performance comes from classical pre- and post-processing, so results reflect a hybrid pipeline rather than pure quantum advantage.
insights.locator: Prior to circuit synthesis, an automated preprocessor

insights.claim: In Qiskit Functions Catalog evaluations on IBM Heron hardware, replacing variational training with iterative warm-starting cut QPU compute times from 130-200 seconds to roughly 30 seconds on medium and large problem tiers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A roughly 4-7x reduction in billable QPU time materially improves the economics of quantum optimization on IBM's cloud.
insights.quote: reduced QPU compute times from 130 to 200 seconds down to roughly 30 seconds
insights.locator: In Qiskit Functions Catalog evaluations on IBM Heron hardware

insights.claim: On a hardware-tailored spin glass benchmark with 48 one-hot constraints on the 144-qubit ibm_boston (Heron r3), Aqarios' optimizer found exact optima in 3 of 5 instances and above 99% approximation ratio in the other 2.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Benchmarks are on hardware-tailored instances, which flatter results; treat as feasibility evidence rather than proof of advantage over classical solvers.
insights.quote: Found exact optima in 3 of 5 instances and >99% approximation ratio in the remaining 2.
insights.locator: Aqarios Constrained Quantum Optimizer Hardware Benchmarks

insights.claim: On the 156-qubit ibm_marrakesh (Heron r2), Aqarios' optimizer reached 100% feasible optima on QOBLIB Maximum Independent Set instances (es60fst02: 186 vars/124 qubits in 147 s QPU time; sloane_2dc_128: 128 vars/74 qubits in 106 s QPU time) and on a Karate Club Max-4-Cut (132 vars/132 qubits in 200 s QPU time).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Total runtimes (258-940 s) far exceed QPU time and no classical baseline is reported, so commercial edge versus classical solvers remains unproven.
insights.quote: 100.0% feasible optimum in 147.0 s QPU time (940.2 s total runtime; 25,000 shots).
insights.locator: Aqarios Constrained Quantum Optimizer Hardware Benchmarks
